title: Team Adoption
description: Adoption by team, and whether it is even within one. Defaults to team grouping: a shared dashboard should not open on a ranked list of named developers. Individuals are one filter away for a manager who needs them.

list.name: contributor
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '(unattributed)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos ORDER BY 1
list.label: Contributor

list.name: team
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(t.name, ''), '(unassigned)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(t.name, ''), '(unassigned)') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos r LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = r.contributor LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id ORDER BY 1
list.label: Team

list.name: evidence
list.label: Evidence
list.query: intersected — agent lines survived : intersected,observed — agent edited the files : observed,inferred — from surrounding evidence : inferred,declared — stated only : declared,undetermined — no evidence either way : undetermined

panels.title: Adoption by team
panels.description: Share of each team's commits carrying AI attribution, over the selected range. The question a rollout actually has to answer: whether adoption is even, or one team carrying it. A team low here is a conversation, not a failing — it may be work the tools suit less well.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(c.status = 'assisted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS `adoption %`
FROM whodunit_commits c
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${evidence:raw}' = '__all__' OR c.method = '${evidence:raw}')
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `adoption %` DESC

panels.title: Evidence strength by team
panels.description: How each team's attribution was established, strongest first. A team resting on `declared` is a weaker claim than one on `intersected`, and the difference matters before any figure is quoted upward. Not a quality measure: it reflects which agents a team uses.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       SUM(c.method = 'intersected') AS `intersected`,
       SUM(c.method = 'observed')    AS `observed`,
       SUM(c.method = 'declared')    AS `declared`
FROM whodunit_commits c
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE c.status = 'assisted'
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `intersected` DESC

panels.title: Where the AI work is happening
panels.description: Each team's share of all AI-assisted commits. A pie because this genuinely is parts of a whole, unlike the adoption rate beside it — those are four independent percentages that sum past 200. A large slice means volume, not enthusiasm: a big team will dominate it at any adoption rate.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       COUNT(*) AS `assisted commits`
FROM whodunit_commits c
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE c.status = 'assisted'
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `assisted commits` DESC

panels.title: Agent mix by team
panels.description: Which assistants each team actually runs, counted from agent edits. Teams standardising on different tools is worth knowing before a licence decision, and it explains evidence-strength differences above — not every agent leaves a transcript to match against.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       SUM(e.agent = 'claude-code') AS `claude-code`,
       SUM(e.agent = 'codex')       AS `codex`,
       SUM(e.agent = 'agy')         AS `agy`
FROM whodunit_events e
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = e.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, e.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, e.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `claude-code` DESC

panels.title: Work mix by team
panels.description: What each team spends its commits on, by Conventional Commit prefix. A team heavy on `fix` against one heavy on `feature` is doing different work, which is the context an adoption percentage lacks on its own. Labels describe what commits were called, not what actually broke.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       SUM(c.purpose = 'feature')  AS `feature`,
       SUM(c.purpose = 'fix')      AS `fix`,
       SUM(c.purpose = 'docs')     AS `docs`,
       SUM(c.purpose = 'test')     AS `test`,
       SUM(c.purpose = 'refactor') AS `refactor`
FROM whodunit_commits c
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `feature` DESC

panels.title: Adoption by team, over time
panels.description: Each team's AI-assisted share per period, so a rollout can be seen spreading rather than inferred from one number. A flat line on a team that adopted months ago is steady state; a flat line on a new team is a stalled rollout.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(c.committed_at / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400) AS `time`,
       COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `metric`,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(c.status = 'assisted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS `value`
FROM whodunit_commits c
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(c.committed_at / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400),
         COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `time`

panels.title: Is adoption even within each team?
panels.description: The spread between the highest and lowest adopter on each team. A team at 60% made of two people at 90% and two at 30% needs a different conversation from one where everybody sits at 60%, and the team average hides which it is.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT team, `people`, `team adoption %`, `lowest %`, `highest %`,
       `highest %` - `lowest %` AS `spread`
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS team,
         COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)) AS `people`,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(c.status = 'assisted') / COUNT(*)) AS `team adoption %`,
         MIN(p.pct) AS `lowest %`, MAX(p.pct) AS `highest %`
  FROM whodunit_commits c
  LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
  JOIN (
    SELECT COALESCE(wi2.canonical, c2.contributor) AS person,
           ROUND(100.0 * SUM(c2.status = 'assisted') / COUNT(*)) AS pct
    FROM whodunit_commits c2
    LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi2 ON wi2.alias = c2.contributor
    WHERE c2.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
      AND c2.contributor IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY COALESCE(wi2.canonical, c2.contributor)
  ) p ON p.person = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
  WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
    AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
  GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
) x ORDER BY `spread` DESC

panels.title: Adoption within the team
panels.description: Each person's AI-assisted share, grouped by team. Deliberately a distribution rather than a ranked table: the question is whether a team is even or carried by one person, not who is top. Select a Team above to narrow it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CONCAT(SUBSTRING_INDEX(COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor), '@', 1),
              ' · ', COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')) AS `person`,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(c.status = 'assisted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS `adoption %`
FROM whodunit_commits c
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE c.contributor IS NOT NULL
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY CONCAT(SUBSTRING_INDEX(COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor), '@', 1),
                ' · ', COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)'))
ORDER BY `adoption %` DESC

panels.title: How each team works with the agent
panels.description: Sessions grouped by how many tool calls they made: a conversation, a working session, or a task handed over. Says how the tooling is used, not how well — a team weighted to chat may be doing design work that suits it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       SUM(s.tool_calls < 10) AS `chat · under 10 calls`,
       SUM(s.tool_calls >= 10 AND s.tool_calls < 50) AS `working · 10-49`,
       SUM(s.tool_calls >= 50) AS `agentic · 50+`
FROM whodunit_sessions s
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `team`

panels.title: Which model each team runs
panels.description: Sessions per model. Only agents that report one appear — agy reports no model at all, so its sessions are absent here rather than bucketed as unknown. A team on a cheaper model at similar output is a finding worth checking.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       SUM(s.model = 'claude-opus-4')   AS `claude-opus-4`,
       SUM(s.model = 'claude-sonnet-4') AS `claude-sonnet-4`,
       SUM(s.model = 'gpt-5-codex')     AS `gpt-5-codex`
FROM whodunit_sessions s
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE s.model IS NOT NULL AND s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `team`

panels.title: How much autonomy each team grants
panels.description: The permission mode sessions ran under. `plan` reviews before acting, `acceptEdits` applies edits without asking, `bypassPermissions` asks nothing. A team's position here is a trust decision they have made, and it explains throughput differences elsewhere.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       SUM(s.permission_mode = 'plan')              AS `plan`,
       SUM(s.permission_mode = 'default')           AS `default`,
       SUM(s.permission_mode = 'acceptEdits')       AS `acceptEdits`,
       SUM(s.permission_mode = 'bypassPermissions') AS `bypassPermissions`
FROM whodunit_sessions s
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE s.permission_mode IS NOT NULL AND s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `team`

panels.title: Reasoning effort, where the agent reports it
panels.description: Effort per team, from the agents that report it — Codex alone does, so this panel covers a subset by design and is not a gap. Higher effort spends more tokens on the same task, which is the lever behind cost differences between teams running the same work.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`,
       SUM(s.effort = 'low')    AS `low`,
       SUM(s.effort = 'medium') AS `medium`,
       SUM(s.effort = 'high')   AS `high`
FROM whodunit_sessions s
LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor
LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor)
LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id
WHERE s.effort IS NOT NULL AND s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND ('${team:raw}' = '__all__' OR COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)') = '${team:raw}')
  AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__'
       OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = '${contributor:raw}')
GROUP BY COALESCE(t.name, '(unassigned)')
ORDER BY `team`
